messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — P1: Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/chat/completions (global) starting 12:03 UTC. Spike correlates with a config change: route 'chat.default' was updated to hardwire model version 'open-instruct-v2-2026-03'. Possible fallback activity observed.
jordan: ack, oncall here. looking at request traces now. can someone dump routing decision logs for that route?
kevin: pulling runtime traces — the routing_engine picked fallback candidate 'open-chat-v2' for ~18% of requests. that variant is a chat-first model but has a slightly different API surface (system role handling). when runtime attempted to coerce payload we see repeated schema errors and then 502s.
maria: can you paste an example error?
kevin: sure — sample excerpt from runtime log:
```
[12:04:21.123Z] route=chat.default request_id=req-8a21 type=chat model_pin=open-instruct-v2-2026-03 fallback_candidate=open-chat-v2 outcome=ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH details="unexpected role: 'system' -> fallback adapter failed"
[12:04:21.124Z] request_id=req-8a21 result=500 reason="adapter_conversion_error"
```
jordan: ugh. so the pin caused the planner to consider an incompatible variant as fallback. that then triggers errors instead of a graceful fallback. impact: multiple customers hitting chat endpoints got 500s.
support-bot: alerts: 4 enterprise customers affected (acme-corp, brightside, nodal-health, dataflow). error rate peaked at 22% for chat.default; current 5xx ~6%.
maria: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable fallback for chat.default, 2) remove the hardwired model version (unpin) to let stable routing pick compatible variants, 3) notify customers. who can flip the route config now?
jordan: i can do 1 & 2. applying via admin API.
kevin: note — disabling fallback is safer than redirecting to a different variant until we confirm interface compatibility. good call.
jordan: running command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/chat.default/config -d '{"fallback_policy":"none","model_pin":null}'
```
jordan: applied cfg change id=cfg-2026-03-1875 response: `{"status":"ok","applied":true,"cfg_id":"cfg-2026-03-1875"}`
maria: watching metrics — 2 minutes after change 5xx dropped from 22% -> 3.1%. good.
support-bot: acme-corp support ticket #4352 updated: they confirm errors subsided on their end. :thumbsup:
kevin: root cause hypothesis: our fallback selection logic trusts "compatibility_tags" on model manifests, but "hardwire/pin" was bypassing interface compatibility check. planner allowed any variant with matching performance profile even when API surface mismatched.
samir: do we have a quick test we can add to catch this? maybe simulate a pinned unknown variant and validate adapter success before allowing fallback?
kevin: yes — implement runtime preflight: when a pin exists mark the route as requiring "strict_variant_compat=true" OR run a lightweight adapter check at config apply time. i'll put a patch up.
jordan: will keep oncall until metrics stable for 30m. handing off at 13:00 UTC to alex for overnight monitoring. alex: you're on for handoff.
alex: taking over. thanks team. i'll keep the mitigations in place and coordinate postmortem items. please file follow-ups.
maria: customer impact summary for incident report: duration ~00:21 (12:03–12:24 UTC peak), affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, estimated failed requests ~8.2k, P1 severity, impacted enterprise customers listed earlier.
kevin: follow-ups (high priority): [1] enforce interface compatibility on fallback selection + unit tests, [2] add deploy-time preflight for pinned versions, [3] telemetry: emit "fallback_adapter_fail" metric and alert at low threshold, [4] update runbook: recommend "no-fallback" for chat routes until verified.
samir: I'll own #3, adding metric and alert in monitoring.
alex: i'll own the postmortem doc and coordinate timeline + customer comms. tagging product and support for follow-up.
jordan: before handoff — quick sanity check logs:
```
[12:23:58.999Z] route=chat.default 5xx_rate=3.1% requests_per_min=1200 fallback_disabled=true
```
jordan: handing to alex now. thanks all, nice quick mitigation. :heart:
alex: on it. will schedule a canary for the strict-compat change and push RFC for pin semantics.
maria: post-incident note: we should also audit existing route pins for any potential interface mismatch (chat vs instruct vs embeddings). I'll open a ticket.
support-bot: customer notifications: initial acknowledgements sent to impacted customers; follow-up comms will be coordinated in the postmortem.
incident-bot: incident closed -> mitigated (temporary config applied). follow-ups assigned.
